questions.question: When inspecting the windshield before a trip, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check your windshield for cracks or damage that could block your view. Check the wiper arms for proper tension and check the blades for damage or stiff rubber.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.explanation: Watch for signs that other drivers may be impaired. A driver with windows down in cold weather could be impaired from alcohol, drugs, drowsiness, or illness.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Make gentle turns and do not pass other vehicles unless absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Class 1 hazardous materials are:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials include explosives such as ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed to stay safe.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking on both sides, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: You must have a CDL to operate a vehicle designed to carry at least:
questions.explanation: You need a commercial driver license to operate a vehicle designed to hold 16 or more people, including the driver.

questions.question: When coming to a stop, you should apply the brake pedal by:
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these items cannot be transported in the passenger compartment of a bus?
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials in any space where passengers are present.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you think something is wrong.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you see traffic around you and spot any problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a green light at a drawbridge, what should you do?

options.text: You must wait for the light to turn yellow.

questions.explanation: A green signal at a drawbridge means you can cross without stopping. Always slow down and make sure it is safe before crossing.

questions.question: What is a danger when driving near people fixing a broken-down vehicle?

options.text: They are probably watching the road.
They may be focused on the repair and not see traffic.
They do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be focused on the repair and not see traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a broken-down vehicle. They may be focused on fixing the vehicle and not notice nearby traffic.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks a hazard to other drivers?

options.text: Children often run toward them without looking for cars.
They leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward them without looking for cars.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks attract children who may run into the street without checking for traffic. This creates a dangerous situation for drivers.

questions.question: In hot weather, what happens to spots where tar rises to the road surface?

options.text: They have the same grip as the rest of the road.
They have more grip than the rest of the road.

questions.explanation: In very hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery and dangerous.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure while driving?
questions.explanation: Check cargo security within the first 50 miles of your trip, then again every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Leave more space between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between your car and the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your distance from the car in front of you. This gives you more room to stop safely and makes it easier for the other car to pass.

questions.question: Can talking on a hands-free phone while driving be distracting?

options.text: No, it does not distract you.
Only if you are the one speaking.

questions.explanation: Talking on a hands-free phone can distract you as much as a regular phone. Conversations take your mind off driving.

questions.question: What happens to your vehicle's speed when driving downhill?

options.text: It stays the same as on flat road.

questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle faster when going downhill. Slow down before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: What are the rules about refueling a bus with passengers, towing it, or talking to passengers?
questions.explanation: Do not fuel a bus inside a building, tow a bus with passengers on it, or talk to passengers while driving. These are all prohibited.
